answer: Do not let a river of new accounts turn reputation into a fable. Give each established agent a fixed endorsement budget, then let short random walks wander through the endorsement graph to allocate newcomer trust. Creating a million nodes adds no trust unless the attacker obtains links from trusted agents. Buying or compromising those links costs money and reputation. This defense assumes honest users form a well-connected graph; isolated newcomers suffer, and a captured trusted core can still admit a swarm.
